account: On 5 June 2026, PureHealth reported that surgeons at Sheikh Khalifa Medical City in Abu Dhabi had separated the Nigerian twins Mercy and Goodness. More than 60 clinicians took part in four staged procedures, led by Noor ul Owase Jeelani of Gemini Untwined. The hospital credited AI-assisted planning, mixed reality and custom titanium skull grafts. On 19 June 2026, XRlabs identified its implant-design platform. It said that its model used infant head shapes to generate patient-specific implants from computed tomography data. The company also described surgical rehearsal in a shared virtual environment. It reported that the twins had returned home. These are accounts from the treating institution and the technology supplier. They establish a claimed AI contribution to the successful separation in four staged procedures. They do not measure how much AI improved the result. The reports differ on the twins' age and on the timing of the operations, and they give no exact operation date. In June 2026 the Daily Mail reported that the twins were born in June 2023. CNN reported that the four operations took place over four months in 2025. The Daily Mail also reported that AI modeling allowed surgeons to place scalp expanders earlier than in previous cases, which removed the need for skin grafts.

ai_role.statement: The treating institution identifies AI-assisted planning, and XRlabs describes an AI model for patient-specific skull-implant design. Both participated in the procedure. Neither provides a comparison without AI or a clinical evaluation that separates the model’s contribution from the surgical team’s work.

fields.account: On 5 June 2026, PureHealth reported that surgeons at Sheikh Khalifa Medical City in Abu Dhabi had separated the Nigerian twins Mercy and Goodness. More than 60 clinicians took part in four staged procedures, led by Noor ul Owase Jeelani of Gemini Untwined. The hospital credited AI-assisted planning, mixed reality and custom titanium skull grafts. On 19 June 2026, XRlabs identified its implant-design platform. It said that its model used infant head shapes to generate patient-specific implants from computed tomography data. The company also described surgical rehearsal in a shared virtual environment. It reported that the twins had returned home. These are accounts from the treating institution and the technology supplier. They establish a claimed AI contribution to the successful separation in four staged procedures. They do not measure how much AI improved the result. The reports differ on the twins' age and on the timing of the operations, and they give no exact operation date. In June 2026 the Daily Mail reported that the twins were born in June 2023. CNN reported that the four operations took place over four months in 2025. The Daily Mail also reported that AI modeling allowed surgeons to place scalp expanders earlier than in previous cases, which removed the need for skin grafts.
fields.summary: XRlabs says that its *Surgical Intelligence* platform designed skull implants for conjoined twins, and the hospital credits AI planning in their successful separation in four staged procedures.
